title: Cross-Border Failover and Data Residency Intake Runway
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a repeatable intake and routing runway for enterprise customer requests that require cross-border failover, strict data residency, or multi-region failover topologies. The goal is to standardize the triage fields, priority mapping, legal/jurisdiction gating, SLA delta calculation, and runbook outputs so sales, support, and solutions engineering can get a clear, actionable outcome within 5 business days.
background: Over the last two quarters we've seen an uptick in enterprise requests for: a) adding new geographic regions for residency, b) multi-region failover configured for low-latency redundancy across borders, and c) contractual residency constraints tied to procurement. Current intake is ad-hoc — tickets land in support or sales and each team collects different info, leading to long cycles and legal rework. This ticket defines a prescriptive intake runway + decision matrix that can plug into the existing region onboarding funnel.
scope: Includes: intake form fields, priority scoring rules, SLA delta calculator (latency/availability tradeoffs), legal jurisdiction mapping checklist, required infra estimates, and customer response templates. Excludes: implementation project execution (handled by engineering program tickets) and billing/contract amendments (handled by sales operations).
intake_criteria: New region requests, requests that require guaranteed data residency (at-rest or in-transit), cross-border failover requirements, or contractual residency obligations. The intake must capture: customer size, compliance requirement (e.g., GDPR/Sch-XYZ), expected QPS, traffic failover window, RTO/RPO expectations, and whether the request is for hosted/dedicated/private deployment.
prioritization_matrix: Score by: customer ARR (40%), compliance severity/legal blocker (25%), technical feasibility & infra cost delta (20%), strategic market fit (15%). Map scores to priority buckets: Critical (>=85) -> P0/P1 fast-track; Important (60-84) -> P1; Consider (40-59) -> P2; Low (<40) -> P3. For failing over across borders, add an automatic +10 score if the customer has active contracts covering the target region.
acceptance_criteria: Standardized intake form published in Confluence and linked from Support/Sales playbooks
Triage automation rule created: new form submissions create PM ticket and notify infra/legal owners
SLA delta calculator spreadsheet with example outputs for small/medium/large customers
Legal jurisdiction checklist with flags for prohibited data transfer pairs and recommended mitigation patterns
Communication templates for 'assessment started', 'capacity estimate', and 'final decision'
At least two pilot requests processed end-to-end using the runway with documented timings

open_questions: Do we require a signed addendum before we begin provisioning for residency-constrained requests? (Legal input needed)
What is the acceptable decision SLA when infra needs a custom SKU or capacity order (>5 business days?)

notes: We aim for a 5-business-day turn from intake to an initial decision (accept / accept-with-conditions / decline). For complex infra orders that require procurement or ordering, the intake runway should still produce a clear 'next milestone' and expected lead time.
